title: Modi at Delhi Dussehra: Unite, Defeat Enemies, Govern as Ram Rajya
excerpt: At the Ravana Dahan in IP Extension on October 20, Prime Minister Narendra Modi defined India's enemies as forces that harm its honour, divide society and hate its culture, and held up Ram Rajya — no discrimination, equal justice and power as service — as the standard for governance and self-reliant development.
body:
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi used the Vijayadashami celebrations in East Delhi on October 20 to call on all political parties and institutions to unite against forces he said harm India's honour, divide society and hate its culture.
  • He held up Ram Rajya as his governance model: no discrimination, justice and equal opportunity for all, with power defined as service, not rule, and the poor as the first priority.
  • Modi tied Lord Ram's resolve to self-reliance, urging Indians to trust their own resources toward a Viksit Bharat and an Atmanirbhar Bharat.
  • For readers, the tests are practical: whether parties answer the unity call, and whether the Ram Rajya service standard reaches the poorest citizens first.

NEW DELHI — Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday performed the traditional Ravana Dahan in East Delhi and used his Vijayadashami address to deliver two linked messages: the country must identify and defeat what he called its enemies, and those in power must govern by Ram Rajya, where authority exists to serve rather than to rule.

Modi spoke at the DDA Utsav Ground in IP Extension, Patparganj, at celebrations organised by the Shri Ramlila Committee Indraprastha. He opened by bowing to Lord Shri Ram, Mother Janaki and Bajrangbali, saying every corner of India was immersed in Ram and Ramlilas keep Lord Ram's ideals alive. For us, he said, this is not merely a festival; it is the life force of India — a proclamation of the end of tyranny and terror and of the eternal victory of truth over falsehood.

Identify the enemies, and stand together against them

The sharpest part of the address was Modi's definition of the country's enemies. He did not name any individual, party or group. Instead, as ANI reported from the celebrations, he framed the threat in terms of conduct toward the nation itself.

"The forces that harm the honour of the country, the people who divide the society, the mentality of those who hate our culture, these are the enemies of the country. We will have to recognise the enemies of Maa Bharati. We will have to defeat them."

— Narendra Modi, Prime Minister

Modi said ancient seers had taught that all political parties and all institutions should be united against enemies, and he renewed that appeal on Vijayadashami — a nation-first call for unity in the national interest, rather than behind a party.

Ram Rajya as a test of governance

Modi then set out the model he said follows from Lord Ram's life: a system free of discrimination, where everyone receives justice and equal opportunities, and where the purpose of power is not to rule but to serve the welfare of the people. Serving the poor and the marginalised, he said, must remain the highest priority, summed up in treating the public as Janardan — the citizen as God.

India's faith in Lord Ram, he added, rests not only on the defeat of Ravana: Lord Ram faced severe difficulties, yet never left the path of truth and policy. Modi also reiterated the vision articulated at the Pran Pratishtha consecration of the Ram temple in Ayodhya — a journey from Ram to Rashtra, from the deity to the country — to be realised if people remained united in purpose.

Self-reliance, heritage and a developed India

Citing Lord Ram before the ocean, with Lanka far away, Modi said Ram awakened the collective strength of the people, made public participation his source of strength and turned an apparently impossible goal into a possible one using the resources at hand. The lesson today, he said, is to trust one's own resources, turn resolve into strength and forge solutions through hard work, rather than rely on others in a crisis — the mantra behind the goals of a Viksit Bharat and an Atmanirbhar Bharat.

Modi connected progress to self-respect rooted in heritage, noting that more than 650 ancient artefacts and idols had been brought back to India over the past 12 years, and citing UNESCO recognitions, including Diwali's inclusion on the Intangible Cultural Heritage list. Earlier in the day, in a post on X, he had wished that the festival imbue everyone's resolve with renewed strength and enrich every life with happiness, prosperity and success.

What to watch next

Modi named no opponents, so the immediate question is response: whether opposition parties treat the unity appeal as a shared national call or contest the framing of unnamed enemies. The governance claim is also measurable in Modi's own terms — equal treatment, equal opportunity and service to the poor first. In a separate Delhi celebration the same day, President Droupadi Murmu attended Dussehra events at Dwarka Sector 10, where Chief Minister Rekha Gupta urged people to follow Lord Ram's ideals against social evils including corruption, discrimination and atrocities against women.
